findings.body: CryptoIntegration.init() invokes order() while sorting providers and fails with AbstractMethodError, preventing crypto initialization and application startup.

findings.root_cause: A new abstract method was added to an existing public provider interface.

findings.title: Keep the public CryptoProvider SPI binary-compatible
findings.trigger: An application has a CryptoProvider implementation compiled against the previous version of this public ServiceLoader SPI and upgrades the common library without recompiling that provider.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 44 adds 'int order();' as a new abstract method to the public CryptoProvider interface. The suggested fix (default method) is appropriate.

pr.body:
…tory

closes #33831

This is the Keycloak main part for solving the https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/32962 and adding the related changes in the authz-client on the Keycloak side, which can then be later synced to the keycloak-client repository. 

In the end, I am using approach (2) from https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/32962 with adding the method `order()` to `CryptoProvider`, which allows to have multiple instances of `CryptoProvider` on classpath (Keycloak testsuite still uses the `DefaultCryptoProvider` as before this PR).

raw_findings.body: Provider selection now depends on ServiceLoader/classpath iteration order instead of failing fast; the non-FIPS provider can be selected in a FIPS deployment, silently bypassing the intended crypto implementation.
raw_findings.failure_mode: An ambiguous security-provider configuration is silently accepted and may initialize the wrong crypto implementation.
raw_findings.impact: Provider selection now depends on ServiceLoader/classpath iteration order instead of failing fast; the non-FIPS provider can be selected in a FIPS deployment, silently bypassing the intended crypto implementation.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new ordering logic removes the multiple-provider failure without handling equal-priority providers.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: After sorting, reject multiple providers tied for the highest order (or assign and enforce an unambiguous mode-specific priority) rather than returning the first tied provider.
raw_findings.title: Reject ambiguous highest-priority crypto providers
raw_findings.trigger: A runtime classpath exposes two full crypto providers with the same order, such as DefaultCryptoProvider and FIPS1402Provider, and CryptoIntegration.init() is called.

raw_findings.body: The conversion ignores the suffix and verifies only the valid prefix, accepting a malformed non-canonical JWS signature instead of rejecting it.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Signature verification normalizes and accepts trailing data that is outside the signed ECDSA representation.
raw_findings.impact: The conversion ignores the suffix and verifies only the valid prefix, accepting a malformed non-canonical JWS signature instead of rejecting it.
raw_findings.root_cause: The raw-to-DER conversion copies only the expected r and s bytes without validating that the input contains exactly those bytes.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Before copying, require signature.length == signLength and throw IOException (or return verification failure) for any other length.

raw_findings.body: The ES384 and ES512 tests can remain green because all cases sign with the provider-default EC curve; changing only the digest algorithm and requested output width does not exercise signatures generated by secp384r1 or secp521r1.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Coverage does not validate interoperability for the actual ES384 and ES512 key sizes.
raw_findings.impact: The ES384 and ES512 tests can remain green because all cases sign with the provider-default EC curve; changing only the digest algorithm and requested output width does not exercise signatures generated by secp384r1 or secp521r1.
raw_findings.root_cause: A single unparameterized EC key pair is reused for every advertised ECDSA algorithm.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Generate a key pair per test using ECGenParameterSpec("secp256r1"), "secp384r1", and "secp521r1" respectively, and verify the converted DER signature with the corresponding public key.

raw_findings.trigger: The conversion mishandles 48-byte ES384 or 66-byte ES512 components, including leading-sign-byte and padding cases specific to larger curves.

finding.trigger: A runtime classpath exposes two full crypto providers with the same order, such as DefaultCryptoProvider and FIPS1402Provider, and CryptoIntegration.init() is called.
finding.verifier_reason: The patch shows DefaultCryptoProvider returns order()=0, FIPS1402Provider returns order()=100, and AuthzClientCryptoProvider returns order()=-1. These are distinct values, so providers with the same order is not a realistic trigger. The built-in providers have unambiguous priorities by design.

finding.impact: The conversion ignores the suffix and verifies only the valid prefix, accepting a malformed non-canonical JWS signature instead of rejecting it.

finding.title: Reject ECDSA signatures with trailing raw bytes
finding.trigger: An ECDSA verifier using this provider receives a JWS raw signature whose first signLength bytes form a valid signature but which has one or more extra bytes appended.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that trailing bytes are silently accepted is incorrect. The conversion copies exactly signLength bytes (len for r, len for s) and produces a DER encoding of those values. The JCA Signature.verify() then validates the DER signature against the public key; extra trailing bytes in the original input do not affect the cryptographic verification result. No security bypass is demonstrated.
